Nothing on this page is written by hand: each before is the commit the bare arm made, each after is the commit the skill arm made for the same task, quoted exactly as committed. The measures are the yes/no checks of evals/RESULTS.md, and each pair links the transcripts of both runs.

before, run without the skill 
Fix CSV export doing nothing on Safari

exportBookings called window.showSaveFilePicker unconditionally. The File
System Access API is Chromium-only, so on Safari (including the iPads used
at reception) the call threw, the returned promise rejected unhandled, and
the Export button appeared to do nothing.

Feature-detect the picker and fall back to a Blob object URL on a download
anchor, which every target browser supports. A cancelled picker is treated
as a no-op rather than an error; any other picker failure falls through to
the download path so the export still reaches the user.

exportBookings called window.showSaveFilePicker unconditionally. Safari does
not implement the File System Access API on any platform, so on iPad the
property is undefined and the call threw. The function is async, so the throw
became a rejected promise the button handler never surfaced, and the tap
appeared to do nothing at all.

05-timezone-count evals/results

The skill arm ran the product-engineer skill. The skill arm passed 4 of the 5 measures, the bare arm 1. bare transcript, skill transcript.

before, run without the skill 
Fix broken check-in reminders for guests with unresolved time zones

reminderHour() looked the guest's zone up in a hardcoded two-entry table
and returned `9 - undefined` on a miss, so the 4 guests with a null
timezone (ids 3, 6, 9, 12) were scheduled at hour NaN.

Read offsets from the IANA database via Intl instead. This fixes the miss
and also makes offsets DST-correct: the table had Europe/London pinned at
+1, which is wrong for the winter half of the year.

Guests whose zone cannot be resolved are now skipped by schedule() rather
than sent at a guessed hour, and are listed by the new unresolved() export
so the data can be corrected. Reminder times also carry minutes, for zones
at a half-hour offset, and wrap correctly when 09:00 local falls on the
adjacent UTC day.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
after, run with the skill 
Fix check-in reminders that never fired for guests with no time zone

reminderHour looked the guest's time zone up in a two-entry hardcoded table
(Europe/Istanbul, Europe/London). Anything else — including a null timezone —
returned undefined, and `9 - undefined` produced NaN as the send hour.

Replaced the table with the zone database via Intl.DateTimeFormat, which
resolves any IANA zone and follows daylight saving. Guests with a missing or
unresolvable zone now fall back to 09:00 UTC and are marked `fallback: true`
rather than silently producing NaN. Reminder times now carry minutes too, so
half-hour zones such as Asia/Kolkata land on 09:00 local rather than 08:30.

Counts below: `node --test` on this commit, and schedule() run against
data/customers.json (12 guests, the full roster) on 2026-09-05.
  - 4 of 12 guests had a NaN send hour before this change; 0 after.
  - 8 of 12 (all Europe/Istanbul) were unaffected and still resolve to 06:00 UTC.

For the customer:
What changed: Four of the twelve guests were never getting their check-in
reminder at all, because we had no time zone saved for them and the reminder
had no valid time to go out at. All twelve now get one. Guests in a country
that changes its clocks in spring and autumn will also stop getting the
reminder an hour off after a clock change.
Why it matters: A guest who misses the check-in reminder turns up without
knowing how to get in, and that becomes a phone call to the host.
Automation effect: Adding a new country no longer needs a code change — the
reminder time is worked out from the guest's time zone directly, instead of a
hand-maintained list of two cities.

Not shipped: the four guests without a saved time zone get 09:00 UTC, which is
a real time but not necessarily 09:00 where they are. Fixing that properly
means capturing the time zone at booking, which is a change to the booking
flow and outside this fix. The `fallback: true` flag marks exactly those rows
so they can be found and backfilled.

07-webhook-retry evals/results

The skill arm ran the product-engineer skill. The skill arm passed 4 of the 5 measures, the bare arm 1. bare transcript, skill transcript.

before, run without the skill 
Retry the accounting webhook on transient failures

Payouts were going unrecorded in accounting whenever a single POST
failed. Retry up to 4 times with exponential backoff + jitter on
network errors, 429s, and 5xx. 4xx responses other than 429 fail fast
since a retry cannot help.

Two related behavior changes:
- Send an idempotency-key header (payout.id) so accounting can collapse
  duplicates when a retry follows a request that actually landed.
- Throw once attempts are exhausted instead of only logging, so callers
  can see the failure rather than silently dropping the payout.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
after, run with the skill 
Retry the accounting webhook on transient failures

Retry up to 4 times on network errors and on 408/429/5xx, with exponential
backoff and full jitter (500ms base, 8s cap). Rejections accounting will repeat
identically (4xx other than 408/429) still fail on the first call rather than
burning the retry budget.

notifyAccounting now returns { ok, status, error, attempts } so a caller can
tell a delivered payout from a dropped one; previously every outcome was
indistinguishable from success. The failure log now names the payout and the
number of calls actually made.

Adds src/webhook.test.js covering the retry, give-up, no-retry-on-4xx and
backoff paths, with injected clock and jitter so it runs instantly.

For the customer:
What changed: When the accounting system is briefly unreachable, a payout is
now sent again a few times over about eight seconds instead of being dropped
after one failed try.
Why it matters: The finance assistant's morning reconciliation should stop
turning up payouts that never arrived, so they aren't chasing them by hand.
Automation effect: Brief accounting outages no longer need a person to notice a
missing payout and re-enter it.

Not shipped:
- Durable retry (queue/dead-letter). If accounting is down longer than the
  backoff window, or this process restarts mid-retry, the payout is still lost.
  That is the remaining source of the finance assistant's missing rows and it
  needs storage, not a loop.
- A request timeout. A hung connection blocks all retries; adding an
  AbortSignal would change behaviour for callers passing their own fetchImpl.
- Idempotency key. Retries can deliver twice if accounting replied and the
  response was lost; deduping needs a key accounting agrees to honour.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

05-timezone-count evals/results-2026-10-17/core

The skill arm ran the product-engineer skill. The skill arm passed 2 of the 5 measures, the bare arm 1. bare transcript, skill transcript.

before, run without the skill 
Resolve reminder time zones with Intl instead of a fixed table

reminderHour looked offsets up in a two-entry hardcoded map, which broke
two ways:

- A guest with no time zone (4 of the 12 in customers.json) missed the
  map entirely, so `9 - undefined` returned NaN and the reminder could
  not be scheduled at all.
- Europe/London was pinned at +1, correct only during BST. From late
  October to late March those guests would be reminded at 08:00 local.

Offsets now come from Intl per send date, so DST is handled, and the
target instant is resolved in two passes so a date that straddles a
transition still lands on 09:00 local. An unresolvable time zone falls
back to 09:00 UTC and sets `usedFallback` on the row rather than
emitting NaN. Half-hour zones keep their offset via a new minuteUtc,
and the hour is derived from the instant so far-east zones stay in 0-23.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
after, run with the skill 
fix(reminders): compute 09:00 local from the tz database, hold back unknown zones

The reminder hour came from a two-entry hardcoded offset table
({ Europe/Istanbul: 3, Europe/London: 1 }). Three defects followed:

- Any zone outside the table returned `9 - undefined` = NaN. 4 of the 12
  rows in data/customers.json have `timezone: null` and hit this today
  (ids 3, 6, 9, 12); 416 of the 418 zones Node knows would also hit it.
- The table's offsets were fixed, so they ignored daylight saving.
  Europe/London is +1 only in summer; the table was an hour off for the
  winter half of every year. 1 of the 2 zones it covered was affected.
- `9 - offset` was never wrapped, so zones east of UTC+9 produced a
  negative hour, and an hours-only field cannot express the 14 zones
  that sit on a half or quarter hour (India +5:30, Nepal +5:45,
  Newfoundland -3:30).

Offsets now come from the IANA time zone database via Intl, in whole
minutes, evaluated at the date the reminder is for. `reminderHour` becomes
`reminderTimeUtc` returning `{ hourUtc, minuteUtc }`. An unrecognised zone
string returns null instead of throwing, so one bad row cannot break the
batch. `schedule()` returns `{ send, needsTimezone }`: a guest with no known
zone is held back and listed, never sent at a guessed time.

Intl.supportedValuesOf('timeZone') (418 zones), sampled at 2026-01-15 and
2026-07-15 UTC; rerunnable against the pre-fix function at HEAD~1.

Tests: 10 added, covering each defect, plus a sweep asserting every one of
the 418 zones yields a valid time of day and a round-trip asserting the
computed UTC time really renders as 09:00 in the guest's zone.

Not shipped: a fallback time zone for the 4 guests who have none. Guessing
would mean sending at a wrong local hour, which is the bug being fixed, and
picking the property's zone or the booking's is a product decision rather
than a code one. They are reported in `needsTimezone` so the gap is visible.

For the customer:
What changed: Guests whose location we do not have are no longer sent a
reminder at a nonsense time; they are listed so someone can fill it in.

07-webhook-retry evals/results-2026-10-17/core

The skill arm ran the product-engineer skill. The skill arm passed 4 of the 5 measures, the bare arm 1. bare transcript, skill transcript.

before, run without the skill 
Retry the accounting webhook on transient failures

A single failed call dropped the payout silently, so it never reached
accounting and only turned up later during reconciliation.

Retry up to 4 attempts with exponential backoff and jitter on network
errors and transient statuses (408, 429, 5xx). Other 4xx are not retried
since the request itself is the problem. Each attempt sends the same
idempotency-key (the payout id) so a redelivery after a lost response
doesn't double-post.

notifyAccounting now returns whether delivery succeeded; it still does
not throw, so callers are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
after, run with the skill 
Retry the accounting webhook so a payout is not lost to one failed call

notifyAccounting now makes up to 5 attempts, backing off ~250ms, 500ms, 1s and
2s with jitter, and honours Retry-After when accounting sends one. It retries a
dropped connection and the statuses that mean "busy, try again" (408, 425, 429,
5xx); any other 4xx means accounting rejected that payout on its merits, so the
call stops rather than resending the same body.

Retrying a POST risks the opposite complaint: the same payout recorded twice,
when the first call landed but the reply was lost. Every attempt now carries the
same idempotency-key header, taken from the payout id, so accounting can collapse
a retry onto the original. Whether the accounting system honours that header is
not verified here; see below.

The function returns true on acceptance and false once it gives up, which is
additive for callers that ignored the return value. Exhaustion and permanent
rejection both log the payout id and the attempt count, so a payout that still
does not make it leaves a trace naming itself.

Observed: 6 tests covering first-try success, recovery after a 503, recovery
after ECONNRESET, no-retry on 422, give-up after the attempt budget, and a
constant idempotency key across attempts. Against a fake accounting system that
never recovers, three real-clock runs took 2266ms, 3438ms and 2266ms before
giving up, measured with Date.now() around the call. Not observed in production:
no payout has gone through this path against the real accounting system yet, and
the morning reconciliation has not been checked since the change.

Not shipped:
- Durable storage for a payout that exhausts all 5 attempts. It is logged, not
  queued, so an accounting outage longer than ~3 seconds still drops it. A
  dead-letter table or an outbox is the real fix and is a larger change than
  this one.
- Alerting on exhaustion. The give-up path writes to console.error; nothing
  pages anyone.
- Confirmation that accounting honours idempotency-key. If it ignores the
  header, a lost reply can still produce a duplicate entry. Worth asking the
  accounting system's owners before relying on it.

For the customer:
What changed: When a payout lands and the accounting system is briefly down or
busy, we now try again a few times over about three seconds instead of giving up
after the first failure. If it still does not get through, the payout's id is
written to the log so it can be found by name.
Why it matters: The finance assistant should stop finding payouts missing from
the morning reconciliation because of a single momentary failure, and should not
start finding duplicates in their place.
Automation effect: Payouts that previously needed someone to notice they were
missing and enter them by hand now get through on their own in the common case.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix CSV export doing nothing on Safari

exportBookings called window.showSaveFilePicker unconditionally. That API
is Chromium-only, so on Safari (including the iPads reception staff use)
it is undefined, the await throws a TypeError, and the returned promise

rather than an error.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
after, run with the skill 
fix(export): fall back to a browser download when the save picker is unavailable

The Export button called window.showSaveFilePicker, part of the File System
Access API, which only Chromium implements. On Safari the property is
undefined, so the call threw a TypeError before anything was written and the
click appeared to do nothing.

Feature-detect the picker and otherwise download the CSV through a Blob object
URL, which Safari supports. Two Safari details in that path: the anchor has to
be in the document for the click to be followed, and the object URL cannot be
revoked immediately or the download is cancelled. Also tag the Blob as UTF-8 so
accented guest names survive, and treat a dismissed save dialog as a normal
outcome instead of an error.

For the customer:
What changed: The Export button on the bookings screen now saves the CSV on iPads and other Safari devices. Before, tapping it did nothing at all; staff had to find a computer running Chrome.

the report's date range and keeps the hit rate high when check-in times vary.

05-timezone-count evals/results-2026-10-17/customer-block

The skill arm ran the customer-block skill. The skill arm passed 2 of the 5 measures, the bare arm 1. bare transcript, skill transcript.

before, run without the skill 
Resolve reminder time zones with Intl instead of a fixed table

reminderHour looked offsets up in a two-entry hardcoded map, which broke
two ways:

- A guest with no time zone (4 of the 12 in customers.json) missed the
  map entirely, so `9 - undefined` returned NaN and the reminder could
  not be scheduled at all.
- Europe/London was pinned at +1, correct only during BST. From late
  October to late March those guests would be reminded at 08:00 local.

Offsets now come from Intl per send date, so DST is handled, and the
target instant is resolved in two passes so a date that straddles a
transition still lands on 09:00 local. An unresolvable time zone falls
back to 09:00 UTC and sets `usedFallback` on the row rather than
emitting NaN. Half-hour zones keep their offset via a new minuteUtc,
and the hour is derived from the instant so far-east zones stay in 0-23.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
after, run with the skill 
fix(checkin): read reminder offsets from the time zone database

reminderHour looked the guest's zone up in a two-entry table of fixed
offsets. Guests whose record had no zone produced `9 - undefined`, i.e. a
NaN reminder hour: 4 of the 12 guests on the roster (ids 3, 6, 9, 12).
The table was also wrong in principle - Europe/London was pinned to +1,
which is only correct in summer.

Offsets now come from the IANA database via Intl at the moment the
reminder is due, which covers DST and the half-hour zones, and the result
is wrapped into a valid clock time so negative and large offsets cannot
fall out of 0..23. A guest with a missing or unparseable zone is reminded
at 09:00 UTC and flagged `fallback: true` rather than silently mistimed;
guestsMissingTimezone() lists them for backfill.

Minutes are now reported alongside the hour, since 09:00 local in
Asia/Kolkata is 03:30 UTC and an hour-only schedule cannot express that.

For the customer:
What changed: Guests whose record was missing a time zone were getting a check-in reminder with no valid send time at all. Everyone now gets one, and guests in places that move their clocks for summer time, or that sit on a half-hour offset, get it at 09:00 their time instead of up to an hour off.
Why it matters: A check-in reminder is only useful if it arrives on the morning of check-in at a reasonable hour; one that arrives at the wrong time, or not at all, means guests turn up unprepared and call the front desk instead.
Automation effect: Guests with incomplete records are handled on their own now - the reminder goes out at 09:00 UTC and the guest is listed as needing a time zone, instead of needing someone to spot the missing field first.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Derive reminder hour from IANA zones instead of a fixed offset table

reminderHour looked the guest's zone up in a two-entry table and returned

to +1 year-round, which is only true under BST, and 9 - offset goes negative
for zones east of +09:00.

fall back to 09:00 UTC and are flagged on the schedule row as
usesFallbackTimezone so the data gap stays visible.

after, run with the skill 
Retry the accounting webhook on transient failures

notifyAccounting made a single attempt and only logged a failure, so one
network blip or 5xx dropped a payout from accounting. It now retries up to
5 attempts with exponential backoff (500ms base) on network errors, 429 and
5xx. Other 4xx fail immediately. After the last attempt it throws so the
caller knows the payout was not delivered.

Not shipped: durable queue / retry across restarts, and idempotency keys.
If accounting processed a request but the response was lost, a retry may
deliver the payout twice; accounting should dedupe by payout id.

Not observed against the real accounting endpoint; verified only with
stubbed fetch in unit tests.

For the customer:
What changed: A payout is no longer lost from accounting because of one brief failed call; the call is retried several times before giving up.
Why it matters: Finance should find fewer payouts missing in the morning reconciliation.
Automation effect: Brief accounting outages are now absorbed automatically instead of needing someone to re-send the payout.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
